result.reviewScopeSummary: Follow-up verification focused on prior findings SV-03-01 and SV-03-02, the implementor's updated row-merge and maintenance-count changes, targeted Story 3 regression tests, and the configured `npm run verify-all` gate. The prior no-op fixed-count issue is resolved, and the earlier PI E2E timeout did not reproduce during verifier-run `verify-all`, but same-row stale artifact clobbering remains on the directly touched SQLite row-write path.

priorFindingStatuses.rationale: The update preserves newer higher-trust token metadata, but the same row-write path still overwrites newer derived artifact fields when the stale incoming row lacks that nested artifact. `mergeTurnRowDerivedState` only preserves `lowerBandProjection.tokenCountMetadata` when both current and incoming rows already have `lowerBandProjection` (`src/thread/store/sqlite-thread-store.ts:218-239`), and `mergeChunkRowDerivedState` only preserves lower-band token metadata when both current and incoming rows already have the artifact (`src/thread/store/sqlite-thread-store.ts:242-263`). Direct verifier probes showed a newer turn lower-band projection was removed by a stale row write whose `smooth.lowerBandProjection` was undefined, and a newer chunk detailed artifact was removed by a stale row write whose `lowerBand` was undefined. This keeps the original same-row lost-update risk open for derived artifacts/provenance, even though the token-only regression tests now pass.

`maintainAsyncThread` now captures an initial maintenance snapshot and computes `fixedCount` from debt resolved between the initial and final snapshots (`src/thread/async-thread/services/async-thread-run-service.ts:2417-2431,2537-2597`). The new test `already-clean SQLite background maintenance reports zero fixed rows` asserts a clean run persists `fixedCount: 0`, `skippedCount: 0`, `failedCount: 0`, and `remainingDebtCount: 0` (`tests/thread/sqlite-maintenance-reporting.test.ts:94-128`), and the focused Story 3 test command passed.

openFindings.title: Same-row SQLite maintenance writes still lose newer derived artifact state
openFindings.evidence: The follow-up implementation added token metadata preference merging, but the production row merge still starts from the stale incoming row and only preserves nested token metadata when the incoming row already contains the same nested artifact (`src/thread/store/sqlite-thread-store.ts:218-263`). `writeTurnRows` and `writeChunkRows` then persist the merged full `turn_json`/`chunk_json` row (`src/thread/store/sqlite-thread-store.ts:1553-1730`). Verifier probes reproduced the remaining lost-update shape: after writing a newer `smooth.lowerBandProjection.text`, a stale turn row with `lowerBandProjection: undefined` succeeded and left `finalProjectionText: null`; after writing a newer chunk `lowerBand.detailed.text`, a stale chunk row with `lowerBand: undefined` succeeded and left `finalDetailedText: null`. This can silently erase regenerated projection/lower-band artifact state instead of preserving, retrying, or deferring it.

gatesRun.command: node --import tsx <ad hoc stale turn/chunk artifact preservation probes>

productionPathFindings: No fake adapter, mock runtime path, or placeholder execution path was found in the audited production maintenance row-write flow; the remaining issue is in the real `SqliteThreadStore.writeTurnRows`/`writeChunkRows` production path, where stale full-row persistence can still drop newer nested derived artifacts.
additionalObservations: The implementor-reported PI E2E timeout did not reproduce in this verifier run: `npm run verify-all` completed successfully, including the previously failing status/turn-health E2E.
The new token-field same-row regression tests pass, but they do not cover stale incoming rows that lack a newly generated lower-band projection or chunk artifact.
